summary: Verified Bahasa Indonesia language enforcement across 5 surfaces: private persona, group personas, meeting moderator per-turn summary, meeting moderator live interjection, and end-of-meeting /summary endpoint. All 5 pytest tests PASS. Each reply inspected via heuristic (ID function-word hits vs EN markers) and manual preview; every surface returned content with id_hits >> en_hits=0. Regression (200 OK, SSE streaming, meeting_notes task auto-created on /summary) also verified.
critical_code_review_comments: chat.py language directive in _persona_system is well-placed (first line + trailing reminder). Moderator per-turn, interjection, and /summary endpoint all consistently prepend 'You MUST write entirely in {lang_name}'. No regressions found.

Minor: assistant fallback error message in chat.py:198 is hardcoded Indonesian ('Maaf, terjadi gangguan...'). Not a language-enforcement bug, but will not localize if user switches conversation_language. Low priority.
test_credentials: demo@aivora.ai / demo123456 (settings.conversation_language forced to 'id' via PATCH /api/me/settings before each test)
seed_data_creation: Session-scoped fresh meeting created via POST /api/conversations {persona_ids:[2], type:'meeting', title:'TEST_meeting_lang'} and reused across moderator/interject/summary tests to satisfy turn-parity for interjection.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Language enforcement verified end-to-end for 'id'. Test file test_language_enforcement.py uses heuristic lexical detection (ID_MARKERS vs EN_MARKERS) and must be run serially (fresh_meeting_cid fixture is session-scoped and depends on prior tests populating messages before /summary). pytest.ini runs with xdist loadscope by default - that worked for us (single worker). Full suite runtime ~90s. For other target languages, extend LANG markers accordingly.
